mechanism: GZR33 is an investigational long-acting basal insulin analog and insulin receptor agonist. Gan & Lee describes GZR33 as a Class 1 innovative long-acting daily basal insulin that extends duration by increasing human serum albumin affinity through an OEG and 22-carbon fatty diacid side chain attached to human insulin.
phase: Phase 1 for assigned Type 1 Diabetes record; broader GZR33 program has entered Phase 3 in China for Type 2 Diabetes
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT07242664 as a recruiting Phase 1 randomized double-blind crossover clamp study in adults with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitis, with estimated enrollment of 12, actual start October 13, 2025, estimated primary completion February 28, 2026, estimated completion April 15, 2026, and no posted results. Separate GZR33 records show a completed Phase 1 healthy-subject study, a Phase 2 GZR101/GZR33-70 Type 2 Diabetes study, and a Phase 3 China Type 2 Diabetes study comparing once-daily GZR33 with insulin degludec.
expected_launch_window: Type 1 Diabetes: 2031+; broader China Type 2 Diabetes program could be earlier if Phase 3 succeeds
clinical_summary: The assigned Type 1 Diabetes study is a small steady-state clamp trial intended to estimate GZR33 relative potency versus insulin degludec and evaluate pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability. Public efficacy data in Type 1 Diabetes are not yet available. Program-level differentiation rests on a company-described longer-duration, lower-fluctuation basal insulin profile versus daily degludec and broader development progress, including a 350-patient Phase 3 Type 2 Diabetes trial in China with HbA1c change at 26 weeks as the primary endpoint. Until human comparative outcomes are posted, differentiation should be treated as incremental rather than disruptive.
safety_summary: NCT07242664 has no posted results. The assigned trial excludes participants with recurrent severe hypoglycemia, hypoglycemia unawareness, clinically significant comorbidities, or eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and is designed to assess PK/PD, safety, and tolerability versus insulin degludec. Gan & Lee states earlier studies showed good safety/tolerability, effective glucose control in T2D, and low immunogenicity risk, but detailed public datasets were not found. Basal insulin analog safety expectations include hypoglycemia, medication-error risk, hypersensitivity, injection-site/lipodystrophy reactions, hypokalemia, and potential heart failure risk when used with TZDs.
management_tools: Pharmacy-benefit formulary placement against preferred basal insulin analogs after approval
Quantity limits aligned to labeled dose, prescribed units per day, and package size
Prior authorization or formulary-exception criteria for nonpreferred basal insulin use where plan design permits
Step-through preferred insulin glargine/degludec products where clinically appropriate and legally permitted
Continuation criteria tied to glycemic-control need, hypoglycemia history, and tolerability
Safety edits and counseling for duplicate basal insulin therapy, product mix-ups, and concentration or pen/vial conversion errors
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT07242664.
ClinicalTrials.gov still lists NCT07242664 as recruiting even though its estimated completion date of April 15, 2026 has passed.
No public GZR33 U.S. price, FDA approval, or Type 1 Diabetes registrational timeline was identified.
The most advanced public GZR33 development evidence is in Type 2 Diabetes, not the assigned Type 1 Diabetes indication.
Company claims of longer duration, lower fluctuation, and low immunogenicity risk need peer-reviewed or registry-posted human comparative data.

sources.title: Clamp Study to Estimate the Relative Potency of GZR33 Versus Insulin Degludec at Steady State
supports: Assigned asset record: GZR33 in participants with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitis.
Sponsor is Gan and Lee Pharmaceuticals, USA; study ID is GZR33-T1D-US101.
Recruiting Phase 1 randomized double-blind crossover trial with estimated enrollment of 12.
Study intends to investigate pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, safety, tolerability, and relative potency versus insulin degludec.
GZR33 is described as a long-acting basal insulin analogue.
Actual start October 13, 2025; estimated primary completion February 28, 2026; estimated completion April 15, 2026; no posted results.

sources.title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerance, PK and PD Parameters of GZR33 and GZR101 in Healthy Male Adult Subjects
supports: Completed Phase 1 single-dose study of GZR33 and GZR101 in healthy male adults.
Actual enrollment was 52, with actual completion February 24, 2023.
Primary outcome included adverse events, hypoglycemic reactions, injection-site reactions, labs, ECG, vital signs, physical examination, and local tolerability.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.

sources.title: A Trial Comparing Efficacy, Tolerability, and Safety of GZR101 Injection Once Daily (OD) and GZR33-70 Injection OD
supports: Recruiting Phase 2 Type 2 Diabetes study involving once-daily GZR33 Injection as part of GZR33-70.
Primary outcome is change in HbA1c after 16 weeks.
Secondary safety outcomes include treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and hypoglycemia events through Week 19.

sources.title: Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of GZR33 Injection in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
supports: Separate GZR33 Injection Phase 3 study in Type 2 Diabetes sponsored by Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals.
Randomized open-label parallel-controlled study comparing once-daily GZR33 Injection with once-daily insulin degludec injection.
Estimated enrollment is 350; estimated primary completion April 10, 2027; estimated study completion April 17, 2027.
Primary endpoint is HbA1c change from baseline after 26 weeks; safety endpoints include adverse events and serious adverse events through 27 weeks.

sources.title: Gan & Lee Announces First Subject Dosed in China Phase III Study of Class 1 Innovative Long-acting Basal Insulin GZR33 Injection
supports: Gan & Lee announced first subject dosing in a China Phase III GZR33 Injection study for T2D on April 14, 2026.
The company describes GZR33 Injection as a self-developed Class 1 innovative long-acting daily basal insulin for fasting glucose control.
The China Phase III study is planned for about 350 participants across about 50 centers and compares once-daily GZR33 with once-daily insulin degludec.
Gan & Lee states GZR33 has later Tmax, lower fluctuation, and longer duration than daily insulin degludec and that prior early studies showed good safety/tolerability and low immunogenicity risk.
Gan & Lee states global GZR33 development has entered Phase III and GZR101 has entered Phase II.

sources.title: Pipeline - Gan & Lee Medical Product Information
supports: Gan & Lee describes GZR101 as a premixed dual-insulin compound co-formulating investigational long-acting basal insulin GZR33 and fast-acting insulin aspart.
Pipeline page states GZR33, as a GZR101 constituent, was evaluated for human albumin affinity and T2D animal-model efficacy, with PK and safety profile evaluated in rats and beagle dogs.
Pipeline page states GZR101 completed a first-in-human randomized double-blind placebo-controlled dose-escalation Phase I study in China, including GZR33 safety/tolerability and PK/PD objectives.

sources.title: Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals Begins First-In-Human Trial in China for Investigational drug, GZR101
supports: Gan & Lee describes GZR101 as an ultra-long-acting basal insulin GZR33 plus fast-acting insulin aspart co-formulation.
The first-in-human study evaluated safety, tolerability, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity of GZR101 and its constituent GZR33.
Company rationale included potential smoother glucose control, simpler treatment, improved compliance, and reduced treatment burden for GZR101.

sources.title: DailyMed - TRESIBA (insulin degludec) injection, solution
supports: Insulin degludec is a long-acting basal insulin analog indicated to improve glycemic control in patients with diabetes mellitus.
Adults use Tresiba subcutaneously once daily; Type 1 Diabetes starting basal dose is approximately one-third to one-half of total daily insulin dose.

Warnings and precautions include never sharing pens/needles/syringes, hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia with regimen changes, hypoglycemia, hypersensitivity, hypokalemia, fluid retention and heart failure with TZDs, and medication-error risks.

sources.title: Tresiba List Price and Insurance Coverage Explained
supports: NovoCare lists Tresiba FlexTouch U-100 5 x 3 mL pen list price at $508.43.
NovoCare lists Tresiba FlexTouch U-200 3 x 3 mL pen list price at $610.11 and Tresiba vial 1 x 10 mL at $338.95.
NovoCare states list price is before discounts or rebates and most people with insurance do not pay list price.

sources.title: Prior Authorization Protocol - TRESIBA (insulin degludec)
supports: Commercial payer analog supports prior authorization for Tresiba based on Type 1 or Type 2 Diabetes diagnosis.
Policy states coverage is not authorized for non-FDA-approved indications unless sufficient evidence supports use.
Policy notes Tresiba once-daily dosing, contraindication during hypoglycemia, and long duration of action.

expected_launch_window.value: Type 1 Diabetes: 2031+; broader China Type 2 Diabetes program could be earlier if Phase 3 succeeds
expected_launch_window.method: Used assigned Type 1 Diabetes Phase 1 status, lack of posted results, and the need for later-stage T1D efficacy/safety studies; separately considered China Phase 3 T2D progress as broader asset context.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A Type 1 Diabetes launch is not near-term because the assigned record is an early clamp study. Broader GZR33 development is more advanced in T2D, but that does not establish a Type 1 Diabetes regulatory timeline.

annual_cost_range.method: Used Tresiba as the closest marketed once-daily basal insulin analog. Annualized one to two Tresiba U-100 5 x 3 mL FlexTouch cartons per month at $508.43 per carton: $508.43 x 12 = $6,101 and $508.43 x 24 = $12,202, rounded to whole dollars.
annual_cost_range.explanation: GZR33 has no disclosed price. This analog estimate represents gross list-price drug acquisition only and excludes rebates, discounts, patient cost caps, needles, glucose monitoring, visits, hypoglycemia management, or prandial insulin.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced company-described longer-duration/lower-fluctuation profile and Phase 3 T2D progression against the absence of posted Type 1 Diabetes human efficacy results and the presence of established once-daily basal insulin analogs.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: GZR33 may offer incremental basal-insulin pharmacologic advantages versus degludec, but current public evidence does not yet support a Meaningful or High differentiation rating in Type 1 Diabetes.

budget_impact.method: Assessed chronic basal-insulin use, potentially broad diabetes populations, analog annual list-price range near $6k-$12k, and availability of established formulary/quantity controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient drug cost is material but not specialty-biologic scale, and management would likely fit existing basal-insulin pharmacy-benefit controls.

disruption_risk.method: Weighted early Type 1 Diabetes stage, no posted T1D results, no disclosed U.S. filing plan, and standard insulin analog management pathways against broader T2D Phase 3 program progress.
disruption_risk.explanation: Near-term payer disruption is low for the assigned indication. The asset should be watched for Phase 3 readouts and any U.S. filing signals rather than actively planned now.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to Phase 1 Type 1 Diabetes status, absent results, analog-based pricing, and non-imminent U.S. launch visibility.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor ClinicalTrials.gov updates, China Phase 3 progress, any Type 1 Diabetes Phase 2/3 trial initiation, and pricing or regulatory signals before building active formulary policy.

quality_flags: No direct GZR33 price found; annual cost uses Tresiba list-price analog packaging.
Assigned Type 1 Diabetes record is Phase 1 with no posted results, while the broader GZR33 program has Phase 3 progress in Type 2 Diabetes.
ClinicalTrials.gov status for NCT07242664 may be stale because it remains recruiting despite an estimated study completion date of 2026-04-15.
Gan & Lee's claims of longer duration, lower fluctuation, and low immunogenicity risk are company-reported and need public comparative clinical results.
